facts.fact: CostUnit is one of 'postgres-planner', 'mysql-cost', 'mariadb-cost', or 'none'.
facts.quote: type CostUnit = 'postgres-planner' | 'mysql-cost' | 'mariadb-cost' | 'none';

facts.fact: CostUnit is the unit a dialect's native cost figure is reported in, and cost figures are never compared across dialects.
facts.quote: The unit a dialect's own native cost figure is reported in — never compared across dialects

facts.fact: Costs are not compared across dialects because MariaDB's and MySQL's identically-named `cost` field disagree by three orders of magnitude for a comparable scan (F17).
facts.quote:
MariaDB's and MySQL's identically-named `cost` field disagree by three orders of
 magnitude for a comparable scan

facts.fact: CostUnit 'none' covers SQLite and ClickHouse, which report no cost.
facts.quote: 'none' covers SQLite and ClickHouse, which report no cost.

facts.fact: A plan node's `label` is the node's own kind plus the relation it touches when the dialect names one, e.g. "Seq Scan on t", "SCAN t", or "ReadFromMergeTree default.t".
facts.quote:
the node's own kind plus the
 relation it touches, when the dialect names one.

facts.fact: A plan node's optional `detail` is the dialect's own condition/filter text verbatim: Postgres's Filter, MySQL/MariaDB's attached_condition, ClickHouse's Indexes[].Condition, or SQLite's detail string.
facts.quote:
The dialect's own condition/filter text, verbatim (Postgres's Filter, MySQL/MariaDB's
 attached_condition, ClickHouse's Indexes[].Condition, SQLite's detail string).

facts.fact: A plan node's `metrics` holds every other field the dialect reported as label/value pairs, so nothing the server said is discarded even without a typed slot.
facts.quote:
Every other field that dialect reported, projected as label/value pairs — nothing the server
 said is discarded

facts.fact: Per D14, `estimatedRowsRead` is the max estimated-rows-read over the plan's scan-type nodes for postgres/mysql/mariadb, or ClickHouse's EXPLAIN ESTIMATE sum.
facts.quote:
max estimated-rows-read over the plan's own scan-type nodes (postgres/mysql/mariadb),
 or ClickHouse's EXPLAIN ESTIMATE sum.

facts.fact: `estimatedRowsRead` is absent on SQLite because SQLite reports no estimate at all.
facts.quote: Absent on sqlite — it reports no estimate at all.

facts.fact: The plan's `issues` is a whole-plan roll-up of every node's issues, deduplicated by code, and is what the panel lists above the tree.
facts.quote:
Whole-plan roll-up of every node's own issues, deduplicated by code — this is what the panel
 lists above the tree.

facts.fact: `overThreshold` is true only when estimatedRowsRead exists and meets or exceeds the configured threshold.
facts.quote: True only when estimatedRowsRead exists and meets/exceeds the configured threshold

facts.fact: D19's auto-explain warning triggers on `overThreshold || issues.some(i => i.severity === 'warn')`, because a structural issue such as a full scan can fire with no row estimate (SQLite).
facts.quote:
D19's
 auto-explain warning trigger is `overThreshold || issues.some(i => i.severity === 'warn')`

facts.fact: `raw` is the exact EXPLAIN text the server returned.

facts.fact: SQLite has no single EXPLAIN blob, so the SQLite parser reconstructs `raw` as one line per row in the same id/parent/notused/detail shape it received.

sqlite has no single blob, so its own parser
 reconstructs one line per row in the same id/parent/notused/detail shape it received.
